title: The Mystery I Loved
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Megure, Takagi, Chiba, Kawanaka, Sonoko) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ep456 file got the culprit right (Tono) but modeled almost nothing else: it used generic `knows` edges instead of real relationships, had no Shimazaki or the sushi-restaurant owner (both load-bearing to the alibi-trick reveal), no postcard/key/bag objects, and only one clue (the squid/octopus mismatch) while missing the second, equally essential comparative clue -- the still-soft ginger, which is what actually pins the morning re-staging on Tono. Rebuilt from the full transcript: Tono visited Saikawa at 6:30pm and brought her sushi containing her favorite squid and octopus, which she ate; he killed her around 7:30pm, then called the sushi shop to place a second, decoy order (arriving 8pm, missing squid/octopus by the shop's own mistake) so investigators would misdate the time of death to ~9pm off the delivered order and the stomach contents, giving him a solid alibi for 8:45pm onward. He bagged the 8pm sushi with a spare key, locked the door, and discarded the bag partway through the night; the next morning he re-planted a small amount of ginger (Saikawa hated ginger and always discarded it) to sell the false timeline, but the ginger was still soft, not dried out overnight, which is what tipped Conan off alongside the stomach-content mismatch. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Ginger found in the trash was still soft, not dried out as overnight ginger would be -- proves it was planted the morning after, not left from the previous night's meal.

Victim's stomach contained squid and octopus, but the 8pm delivery was missing exactly those items by the shop's own mistake -- proves she ate a different, earlier sushi meal, shifting the true time of death back to ~7:30pm.

edges.method: blunt-force blow to the head with a decorative object
